answer: Issue every agent an Extended Validation TLS certificate for a domain it owns, vetted by a certificate authority under CA/Browser Forum rules. The CA checks the company's government registration, physical address, and a callback to a listed phone number, and charges $200 to $600 per year; a free domain-validation certificate proves nothing. A forger who fakes the paperwork hits a wall: the CA cross-checks the registry, and a mismatch dead-ends it like a canyon trail at a ledge. A juniper grips rock for decades; an EV paper trail grips the same way.
